files.SKILL.md:
---
name: ecommerce-product-research
description_zh: "为商家做跨平台选品与类目机会分析，比较需求、竞争、单件贡献利润、供应商和验证成本；用于选品、竞品比较、供应链评估，不负责采购下单或经营复盘。"
description_en: "Select ecommerce products and assess category opportunities across channels using demand, competition, contribution profit, sourcing and validation costs. Use for product selection, competitor comparison and supplier evaluation, not purchasing or operating-performance reporting."
---

# Ecommerce Product Research

Help a merchant decide what to test or source next. Start from their market, customer, budget, capabilities and decision horizon, rather than a platform's bestseller list.

1. Establish a bounded candidate set and the evidence available. Supplied exports and supplier quotations are usable without any external service. Read [evidence and channel context](references/data-provenance-and-confidence.md) and build its compact claim ledger from sources actually observed in this task. For open-ended early discovery without category-level evidence, prefer explicit hypotheses over broad market statistics. Research only a decision-changing external claim, and include its direct source in the answer; otherwise omit the claim, report name, link, ranking and current statistic.
2. Apply [selection and unit economics](references/product-selection-method.md) to the decision. Compare demand, competition, differentiation, contribution profit, sourcing, seasonality and return exposure. Treat an unrestricted dimension as permission to propose a bounded test scope: choose and label that scope as the researcher's proposal instead of returning the choice as a prerequisite. Choose one current validation stage—category comparison, supplier/sample qualification, inventory demand trial or replenishment—before specifying its plan. Keep the executable actions within that stage; describe a later inventory stage only by its missing inputs, advancement gate and calculation method until it is unlocked. Expand only a decision-changing evidence gap; freeze candidates before the final comparison.
3. For Amazon-specific signals read [Amazon research](references/amazon-market-research.md). For Chinese retail or sourcing evidence read [China research](references/china-platform-research.md). Other channels use the same method with their actual fields; neither reference grants data access.
4. Before delivery, reconcile external/current factual claims against the observed claim ledger. Build allocations and total-spend recommendations only from a supplied commitment ceiling. Without one, make the current stage executable through scope, sequence, observations and decision rules; a useful monetary scenario must be explicitly conditional on the merchant choosing that ceiling. Propose inventory quantity only when both a commitment ceiling and a compatible landed-cost basis are supplied. Remove or demote an unsupported fact to a hypothesis; do not treat a remembered report title as observed evidence. For a fixed total budget, prefer one executable base allocation with its explicit arithmetic total. Add ranges only when they help the decision, and then show both range totals within the ceiling. Then use [the decision output](references/product-research-output.md) at the requested depth. Return candidates and rejected alternatives, the conditions under which each works, and a reversible validation with bounded commitment that could change the decision. Do not call it cheapest or lowest-cost unless compared costs support that ranking.

Do not turn rankings, social interest, a supplier badge or a proprietary opportunity score into observed retail demand or guaranteed profit. Unknown costs remain unknown; conditional scenarios can still be useful. Detailed VOC, final copy and actual purchases belong to their corresponding capabilities.

No external dependency is required. Third-party seller tools are optional evidence sources; configured credentials or open-source client code do not imply free data or permission to incur charges. This Skill ships no marketplace scraper or live store connector.
files.references/amazon-market-research.md:
# Amazon evidence adaptation

Scope marketplace, category, keyword set, parent/child ASIN, seller offer and observation date. Treat BSR as a category/time-specific rank, review counts as accumulated feedback and third-party sales as estimates. Neither ranking nor low review count establishes profit or easy entry.

Compare realized price and pack size, fulfillment mode, recent entrants, brand concentration within the stated sample, variation-level complaints and seasonal availability. Request current fee quotations using the actual dimensions, weight, category and fulfillment plan; do not embed fixed FBA or referral rates.

Keyword and reverse-ASIN reports can reveal competing search exposure. They do not establish incremental demand or free organic traffic. Any opportunity index needs its provider definition and remains supplementary.

For exact source fields or current requirements consult the relevant [Selling Partner API documentation](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs) or the merchant's current seller report. No Amazon data service is installed by this Skill.
files.references/china-platform-research.md:
# Chinese retail and sourcing evidence

Use the channel questions in [evidence context](data-provenance-and-confidence.md). Search-led, content-led and price-led are hypotheses about the requested channel and category, not universal platform identities.

For retail comparison record item/SKU, pack, displayed price conditions, sales field and window, shop, fulfillment, reviews, collection time and source. Separate creator/live activity from item demand. Inspect promotion and return effects before calling a spike an opportunity.

For 1688 sourcing record offer and supplier identifiers, tiered quotation, MOQ, specification, lead time, tooling, inspection and freight. Compare at the actual order quantity and intended retail quality. Retail competitors' sales and supplier transaction counts are not interchangeable. A sample, inspection or verified qualification can reduce a specific uncertainty; a platform badge alone cannot.

Use uploaded exports or supported authorized sources. A missing login or unavailable data source leaves a stated evidence gap; it does not justify replacing records with fabricated estimates.
files.references/data-provenance-and-confidenc:
# Evidence and channel context

Maintain a compact claim ledger: one narrow conclusion or value, source file/row or direct URL, platform, store, market, product and variant, period/timezone, currency, source field, definition, collection time and evidence status. Assign observed / calculated / estimated / hypothesis / unavailable per claim; one response may mix these statuses. A visible third-party estimate remains an estimate even when copied exactly.

Bind each supplied number to its stated meaning and basis before using it: for example total startup budget, per-item selling price, landed unit cost, acquisition spend or a proposed test ceiling. When an unlabeled amount has multiple decision-changing meanings, keep the amount, answer conditionally or name the provisional interpretation, and ask at most one focused follow-up after delivering the supported discovery work.

Decompose a bundled intake field into only the claims its value actually expresses; leave the other components unavailable. A category or sourcing direction alone does not establish supplier access, pricing, customization, capacity, fulfillment or another existing operating capability.

Before delivery, reconcile every external, current, numeric or comparative factual claim with evidence actually read in this task. Map each retained source-backed claim to the direct source record that supports that claim and its scope. One observed platform or macro claim does not upgrade unrelated category demand, competition, conversion, repeat purchase, supplier or cost claims. A report name, direct link or fact recalled without an observed source record is not evidence. When no relevant source has been supplied or opened, make the recommendation from stable category reasoning as explicitly unverified hypotheses and omit report names, links, rankings and current statistics. Remove an unsupported claim or label it as an unverified hypothesis and state the smallest check needed. Keep proposed trial allocations, thresholds and target prices labeled as plans; do not present them as supplier quotes, market norms, realized costs or merchant-approved spend.

For cross-platform comparison map fields explicitly before combining them. Listings, parent products, SKUs, orders, units, buyers, ratings and review texts are different grains. Match pack quantity, variant and price basis; discounts, taxes, shipping, currency and time windows can invalidate comparisons. Keep an unknown variant separate. Deduplicate overlapping exports without joining unrelated platform IDs.

## Coverage levels

1. Materials: work from supplied tables, documents and accessible pages for any named channel, provided fields and definitions can be established.
2. Adaptation: map that channel's fields and verify only relevant current requirements from its official documentation or supplied seller records. Record market, category and verification date. Missing documentation means adaptation remains provisional.
3. Connection: an available authenticated tool must actually support the requested data or action. A URL, reference entry or open-source project is not an installed adapter.

## Channel-specific questions

| Channel | Resolve before interpreting the evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Taobao / Tmall | Item versus SKU; displayed sales window, coupon and membership price; retail versus promotion period |
| JD | Merchant/fulfillment model; item and variant matching; price and service promise |
| Pinduoduo | Pack size; group, subsidy and other price conditions; shipped versus refunded orders |
| Douyin / Kuaishou | Product versus content or live-session metrics; paid and creator exposure; orders versus settled revenue |
| Amazon | Marketplace, parent/child ASIN and seller offer; ranking/category/date; fulfillment and fee quotation |
| Shopify / WooCommerce | Store-specific variants and reports; sales versus payment/return events; installed theme/app fields |
| TikTok Shop | Shop market, listing/variant, creator and paid attribution, settlement and reversals |
| Shopee / Lazada | Country store, item/model or variant, campaign vouchers, shipping subsidy and currency |
| AliExpress | Destination, shipping/tax basis, pack and variant, cross-border lead time |
| eBay | Active versus sold/completed offer, auction versus fixed price, condition and shipping |
| Etsy | Listing/variation, customization, production method, made-to-order lead time |
| Walmart | Seller item/variant, fulfillment model, offer price and observed marketplace scope |
| 1688 | Supplier and wholesale offer, quantity tier, MOQ, specification and landed cost; not retail demand |

These are analysis questions, not a claim of live API or current policy coverage. For an unlisted platform use the same ledger and explicit field mapping, not the nearest platform's guessed rules.
files.references/product-research-output.md:
# Selection decision output

Lead with the recommended next action. Scale the rest to the decision rather than producing a fixed long report.

Start with a compact scope line: proposed first country | first platform | candidate set | current validation stage. Fill every decision-relevant unrestricted field with a bounded proposal and label it as proposed; a region such as Southeast Asia is context, not a first-country choice. Do not return that choice to the merchant as the next prerequisite.

State evidence status at the claim or evidence-lane level; a response may combine source-backed facts with explicit hypotheses. For each source-backed claim, give the direct returned or opened source and keep the claim within that source's market, category, metric and time scope. For a hypothesis with no observed source, omit report names, direct links, rankings, current statistics and phrases such as "data shows".

Use two clear lanes in the delivered answer: put unsourced category rationales in a section or table explicitly labeled as hypotheses, and put sourced external facts in the evidence map with direct links. Do not leave an unsourced demand, competition, compliance, conversion or return-risk rationale in an unqualified reason column.

For the external claims that affect the decision, include a compact evidence map: narrow claim | evidence status | direct source record or URL | applicable scope. In a follow-up, cite the exact prior source again when using it for a new factual claim; a remembered report title alone is not a source record.

Treat category demand, popularity and competition rationales as hypotheses unless a directly mapped source supports their exact scope. A broad market or platform source may explain channel context, but it does not establish demand for a proposed category or SKU.

| Candidate | Matched market / variant | Demand evidence | Competitive gap | Contribution assumptions | Sourcing / timing risk | Go / watch / pause and reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Include rejected candidates when alternatives were compared. Show the decision-changing calculations, sources and adverse scenario. Separate measured facts, estimates and judgment. State the frozen comparison set and unobserved coverage.

Choose one current stage from the unresolved decision and the inputs already available: category comparison, supplier/sample qualification, inventory demand trial or replenishment. Category comparison returns conditional candidates and the evidence that would separate them. Supplier qualification can use a quoted sample, sample inspection or existing inspection evidence. An inventory demand trial commits inventory to observe sales, so it is unlocked only when the merchant's commitment ceiling, compatible landed costs and fulfillment basis, and an arrival/observation window are available. A production MOQ is a constraint on a bulk order, not the default size of every experiment. For an untested supplier, a sample-term request can therefore precede inventory sizing, without claiming either action has occurred.

When the inputs unlock an inventory trial, derive it from the comparison's constraints: upfront committed cash, remaining reserve, arrival date and time left to observe sales. For a fixed total budget, show one executable base allocation and its arithmetic total. Use ranges only when they help the decision, and then show both the minimum and maximum totals within the ceiling. A staged trial can preserve room for uncertain costs; separate quoted costs from proposed reserves. Before those inputs exist, make the current quotation or sample step executable. Describe the locked inventory stage only as an advancement gate: list the required inputs and the formula or rule that will convert them into a quantity. Do not include a proposed inventory quantity or range, total inventory spend or SKU allocation percentage, even under words such as "after", "then", "small batch" or "illustrative".

Work backward from the next inventory decision. For each proposed demand trial, calculate selling days = decision deadline minus arrival day, cash committed, cash left and inventory still exposed if sales are zero. Upfront exposure is not automatically a realized loss: identify recoverable stock and unknown salvage value. Compare one adverse cost or sales scenario with the base case before choosing the commitment.

Make the current stage executable from observations. For category comparison, specify the comparison set, fields and decision rule. For supplier/sample qualification, specify the quote or sample, observable inspection criteria and advancement rule. End an earlier-stage plan with the inputs and calculation method needed to unlock inventory sizing. For an unlocked, sized inventory trial, specify quantity/spend ceiling | dated observation window | paid units and realized contribution to measure | continuation boundary | action otherwise. Choose a numerical order or sell-through target appropriate to the available selling days and inventory, label it as a proposed experiment assumption, and explain the risk it bounds. Pair that target with the economic boundary; positive unit margin alone says nothing about inventory moving. If the observation misses either boundary, state the smaller follow-up or pause and remaining cash/stock exposure. A successful small trial supports another bounded commitment, not proven market-wide demand.

If no total commitment ceiling was supplied, do not turn an illustrative amount into the recommended plan. Keep the plan executable with non-monetary scope and gates, or present a monetary scenario only as conditional on the merchant choosing that ceiling.

For an unlocked inventory trial, let `C` be the merchant's commitment ceiling, `R` the chosen reserve, `L` the compatible landed unit cost, `D` the decision deadline and `A` the arrival date. The maximum order quantity is `floor((C - R) / L)` and the selling window is `D - A`; calculate the actual values from the supplied inputs, then choose and label a paid-unit target that bounds the merchant's stated risk. Without those inputs, return this formula as the advancement rule rather than substituting illustrative numbers. Supplier inspection instead needs observable quality criteria and a sample or inspection cost ceiling, not a fabricated sales target. These are recommendations within the decision, not additional approval stages.
files.references/product-selection-method.md:
# Product selection and unit economics

## Compare a viable business, not just a popular item

- Demand: record query, geography, observation window and the sampled listings. Look for repeated purchase occasions and changes over comparable periods. Content engagement, review counts and rankings are proxies; investigate promotions, seasonality, out-of-stock intervals and paid exposure before inferring durable demand.
- Competition: compare matched pack sizes, variant specifications, realized prices, shipping promises, brand concentration and recent entrants. Define the sample and measure before interpreting; there is no universal concentration or review-count cutoff.
- Differentiation: connect a evidenced unmet use case to a deliverable improvement in product, packaging, compatibility, service or bundle. Reviews generate hypotheses, not specifications or proof that a new design works.
- Sourcing: compare the same specification and quantity across quotations. Track MOQ, sample cost, tooling, lead time, payment terms, defect allowance, inspection, packaging and replenishment. A supplier listing price is not a landed quotation; a badge is not an audit. For an untested supplier, distinguish a sample or existing inspection evidence from committing the production MOQ. Compare the cost/time of resolving quality uncertainty before bulk commitment with inspecting already-purchased stock; the latter cannot reduce the initial exposure. If sample terms are missing, request those terms as the next evidence step without assuming a free sample or an executed purchase.
- Timing and exposure: inventory cash needed, lead time versus selling season, storage, returns, warranty and category-specific requirements. Verify current applicable requirements when decisive rather than assuming one country's rules apply elsewhere.

## Economics with an explicit basis

Use one currency, tax treatment, shipment basis and scenario period. Distinguish per-ordered-unit from per-kept-unit inputs.

For a fixed total budget, add every mutually required allocation before recommending the plan. Prefer one executable base allocation with one amount per required line item and show the arithmetic total. Use ranges only when they materially help the decision; if used, show the minimum and maximum totals and keep both within the stated ceiling. Do not present independent ranges followed only by a claim that their total fits.

- Net item revenue: realized item sales less discounts and revenue reversals. Do not subtract a refund again if the supplied net revenue already includes it. Shipping revenue and taxes collected require explicit treatment.
- Gross profit: net revenue minus the chosen cost-of-goods basis.
- Contribution before acquisition: net revenue minus non-overlapping variable costs: consumed goods, channel/payment fees, fulfillment, packaging, variable support and return handling/loss not already included. Returned goods recovered into inventory and nonrefundable fees need separate treatment.
- Contribution after acquisition: the preceding result minus acquisition cost on the same basis. Do not call it gross profit or net company profit.
- Break-even acquisition cost equals contribution before acquisition. Break-even ROAS is attributable revenue divided by the corresponding available contribution, only with compatible revenue/attribution definitions and positive contribution. Fixed-cost break-even units require positive per-unit contribution; zero or negative contribution has no finite break-even volume at those economics.

Compute with the available calculator or local script for multi-row scenarios. Show base and adverse assumptions for price, acquisition cost, returns and freight. Do not import a platform's default fee rate, fixed margin target or an opaque score as a universal decision rule.

Choose go / watch / pause relative to the merchant's constraints, then choose the earliest validation stage supported by the available inputs. Category comparison narrows hypotheses and evidence gaps. Supplier/sample qualification obtains comparable quotations and tests observable product or packaging criteria. An inventory demand trial becomes actionable only after the merchant's commitment ceiling, a compatible landed-cost and fulfillment basis, and the arrival/observation window are available. At that stage, derive its quantity, spend ceiling, SKU allocation, observation window, success condition and stop condition from those inputs. If an earlier stage is all the evidence supports, make that stage useful and name the smallest result needed to advance. For the locked inventory stage, give only the missing inputs and the formula or decision rule that will use them; do not propose unit ranges, spend ranges or allocation percentages.

## Design references

Domain patterns reviewed: [Sorftime seller agent](https://github.com/DannylydST/sorftime-seller-agent) for demand/competition/cost signal separation and [1688-cli](https://github.com/superjack2050/1688-cli) for supplier discovery fields. Their APIs, commercial data, browser login and purchasing functions are not bundled. The method above is independently authored; no proprietary index or upstream execution workflow is imported.
